blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Predicting spatial gene expression from H&E images offers a scalable complement to experimental spatial transcriptomics. However, despite progress in spatial context modeling, how to construct subsequent context from spot states updated by earlier contextual interactions remains underexplored. We introduce HistoLoop, a looped Transformer that formulates prediction as iterative contextual inference. At each refinement step, HistoLoop aggregates the current spot states into context tokens at the corresponding resolution, processes them with a shared spatial Transformer, and retrieves spot-specific contextual information through cross-attention. A memory-mediated update integrates this information into persistent spot states, which are then used to construct context at the next, finer resolution. Under the HEST-Bench HVG50 evaluation protocol, HistoLoop achieves the highest macro-averaged gene-wise Pearson correlation among the compared methods across six cancer-specific tasks spanning five organs in HEST-1K. Ablation studies support the importance of recurrent state refinement and reconstructing context from updated spot states at progressively finer resolutions. Expression-derived clustering further suggests that HistoLoop better captures spatially organized multigene patterns.

blocks.en: Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Spatial transcriptomics (ST) profiles gene expression while preserving its
spatial organization within tissue, enabling the characterization of
spatial heterogeneity, tissue microenvironments, and cell–cell
interactions ( Ståhl et al. 2016 ; Longo et al. 2021 ; Cang et al. 2023 ) .
However, current ST technologies remain costly and experimentally demanding,
which limits their routine application to large cohorts and archival tissue
collections ( Moses and Pachter 2022 ) .
In contrast, hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole-slide images are
routinely acquired in clinical pathology and contain rich morphological
signals associated with underlying molecular states ( Schmauch et al. 2020 ) .
These complementary properties have motivated histology-based spatial gene
expression prediction, which seeks to reconstruct spatially resolved
transcriptomic profiles directly from standard H&E images ( Zeng et al. 2022 ; Xie et al. 2023 ; Chung et al. 2024 ) .

However, the mapping from local histological morphology to molecular state
is inherently context dependent.
Morphologically similar tissue regions may occur in distinct anatomical or
pathological environments and exhibit different transcriptional programs,
such that local appearance alone may provide an ambiguous basis for molecular
prediction.
Spatial context can help reduce this ambiguity by relating local morphology
to its surrounding tissue organization.
This motivates studying both the spatial evidence available to a predictor
and how that evidence is incorporated into spot representations.

blocks.en:
Recent methods have increasingly moved beyond isolated patch-level
prediction by incorporating spatial relationships and broader tissue
context.
Hist2ST models both global and neighboring spatial dependencies through
Transformer- and graph-based modules ( Zeng et al. 2022 ) , while TRIPLEX integrates
target, neighborhood, and global tissue information across multiple
resolutions ( Chung et al. 2024 ) .
More recent hierarchical architectures further propagate information across
spatial scales to enrich local representations ( Wu et al. 2026 ) .
Together, these methods establish the importance of nonlocal context for
histology-based spatial gene expression prediction.
Building on these advances, we ask whether prediction benefits from
coupling spot-state refinement with spatial context reconstruction.
Specifically, updated spot representations can be reused to construct
context at subsequent resolutions, allowing previously incorporated
spatial evidence to influence later contextual messages.
We investigate whether this recurrent coupling provides benefits beyond
access to multiple spatial scales alone.

blocks.en: Related Work
blocks.zh: 有关工作

blocks.en: Histology-Based Spatial Gene Expression Prediction
blocks.zh: 基于历史的空间基因表达预测

blocks.en:
Histology-based spatial gene expression prediction learns molecular
profiles from paired histology and spatial transcriptomics data.
ST-Net ( He et al. 2020 ) established an early image-based prediction framework,
while BLEEP ( Xie et al. 2023 ) and mclSTExp ( Min et al. 2024 ) explored cross-modal
alignment for expression prediction.
DKAN ( Zhang et al. 2026 ) incorporates gene semantic knowledge into this alignment,
and AGL ( Shiku et al. 2026 ) exploits auxiliary genes to improve target-gene
estimation.
Generative approaches provide another direction:
Stem ( Zhu et al. 2025 ) uses conditional diffusion,
STFlow ( Huang et al. 2025a ) models whole-slide expression through flow matching,
and FLAG ( Si et al. 2026 ) combines latent diffusion with spatial graph encoding
and gene foundation model alignment.
MoLF ( Hu and Speidel 2026 ) further addresses pan-cancer heterogeneity through a
mixture-of-experts latent flow.
Broader efforts include HistoPrism ( Hu et al. 2026 ) , which emphasizes
pan-cancer prediction and pathway-level evaluation, and
STPath ( Huang et al. 2025b ) , which learns transferable expression prediction
through large-scale paired pretraining.
These studies advance prediction objectives, biological supervision,
and transfer; HistoLoop focuses on how spatial context is constructed
from evolving tissue representations.

blocks.en: Spatial Context Modeling and Multi-Scale Refinement
blocks.zh: 空间背景建模和多尺度改进

blocks.en:
Spatial modeling connects local morphology to broader tissue organization.
Hist2ST ( Zeng et al. 2022 ) combines global attention with graph-based
neighborhood interactions, while TRIPLEX ( Chung et al. 2024 ) integrates
target, neighborhood, and global features.
HiST ( Wu et al. 2026 ) propagates information through a sparse hierarchical
encoder–decoder with spatial coarsening, recovery, and skip connections.
Spatial dependencies also enter generative models through local spatial
attention in STFlow ( Huang et al. 2025a ) and graph encoding in FLAG ( Si et al. 2026 ) .
These approaches offer different mechanisms for selecting spatial
evidence and propagating it across locations and resolutions.
Building on these advances, we investigate whether coupling persistent
spot-state refinement with context reconstruction provides benefits
beyond access to multiple spatial scales alone.

blocks.en: Pathology Foundation Models
blocks.zh: 病理学基础模型

blocks.en:
Pathology foundation models learn transferable representations from
large-scale histology data.
UNI ( Chen et al. 2024 ) provides general-purpose patch-level features, while
GigaPath ( Xu et al. 2024 ) combines patch-level pretraining with
whole-slide representation learning.
Language supervision further enriches these representations:
CONCH ( Lu et al. 2024 ) learns from histopathology image–caption pairs,
and TITAN ( Ding et al. 2025 ) combines visual self-supervision with
region-level caption and slide-level report alignment.
HEST-Bench ( Jaume et al. 2024 ) evaluates pretrained pathology representations
through spatial gene expression prediction, connecting foundation
model development to this task.
Foundation models provide powerful histological representations, but
they primarily define how visual features are encoded rather than how
spatial evidence should be progressively interpreted during prediction.
HistoLoop builds on pretrained histological features and investigates
this downstream inference process through recurrent spot-state
refinement, complementing advances in pathology representation learning.

blocks.en: Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 实验设置

blocks.en: We evaluate HistoLoop on HEST-1K ( Jaume et al. 2024 ) , covering six cancer types. We construct two data splits while retaining the original hold-out test sets from HEST-Bench, and stratify the remaining samples by cancer type into training and validation sets. For each spot, the model takes a precomputed histology feature extracted by UNI ( Chen et al. 2024 ) from the corresponding H&E image together with its two-dimensional spatial coordinate, and predicts a gene expression profile over a fixed vocabulary of 38,982 genes.
blocks.zh: 我们评价HEST-1K上的HistoLoop(Jaume等人,2024年),涵盖6种癌症类型。 我们在保留HEST-Bench最初的搁置测试设备的同时,将两个数据分割,并按照癌症类型将其余样本分解成培训和验证设备。 对于每个斑点,模型取自UNI(Chen et al. 2024)从对应的H&E图像中提取的预算的神学特征及其二维空间坐标,并在38,982个基因的固定词汇上预测基因表达剖面.

blocks.en: We compare HistoLoop with four recent methods: HiST ( Wu et al. 2026 ) , HistoPrism ( Hu et al. 2026 ) , MoLF ( Hu and Speidel 2026 ) , and STFlow ( Huang et al. 2025a ) . All methods are evaluated using the same UNI features, spatial coordinates, fixed 38,982-gene vocabulary, and data partitions. For each baseline, we follow its official training configuration while keeping the input data and evaluation protocol consistent across methods. For the primary evaluation, we follow the HVG50 protocol of HEST-Bench ( Jaume et al. 2024 ) , using the corresponding predefined panel of 50 highly variable genes (HVG50) for each cancer type. The panel membership is fixed independently of the held-out test data and remains unchanged across splits and methods. For each run, we compute the gene-wise Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) across valid spots for every benchmark gene on each held-out slide, average the resulting values over the benchmark genes and held-out slides to obtain a cancer-level score, and report the mean and standard deviation across five random seeds. The macro average is calculated as the unweighted mean of the six cancer-level mean PCCs.
blocks.zh: 我们比较了HistoLoop与最近四种方法:HiST(Wu等人,2026年),HistoPrism(Hu等人,2026年),MoLF (Hu and Speidel 2026),以及STFlow (黄等人,2025a). 所有方法都使用相同的UNI特征,空间坐标,固定38,982-gene词汇,以及数据分区来评价. 对于每个基线,我们遵循其正式培训配置,同时保持不同方法的投入数据和评价协议的一致性。 对于初级评价,我们遵循HEST-Bench(Jaume等人,2024年)的HVG50协议,使用每种癌症类型的50个高度可变性基因(HVG50)的相应预设面板. 小组成员固定在与搁置测试数据无关的位置上,在划分和方法上保持不变。 每次运行时,我们都会计算出每张挂起滑动幻灯片上每个基准基因的有效斑点的基于基因的皮尔逊相关系数(PCC),在基准基因和挂起滑动幻灯片上的平均结果值,以获得癌症等级的得分,并报告五个随机种子的平均值和标准差。 宏观平均值被计算为6种癌症水平的未加权平均值PCC。

updated spot states. All variants are evaluated using the same protocol
as the main experiments, and the results are summarized in
Table 2 .

blocks.en: Spatial Expression Recovery
blocks.zh: 空间表达恢复

blocks.en: Figure 2: Spatial expression recovery on representative held-out slides.
blocks.zh: 图2 具有代表性的搁置幻灯片上的空间表达恢复。

blocks.en: Aggregate PCC provides a useful measure of spot-level expression agreement, but it does not reveal whether a model recovers the spatial organization of gene expression, such as localized high-expression regions, tissue boundaries, and regional intensity variation. We therefore complement the quantitative results with a qualitative visualization of marker genes. Following the biomarker visualization protocol used in DKAN ( Zhang et al. 2026 ) , we visualize LCN2, GATA3, GPRC5A, and UBE2C, whose relevance to the corresponding cancer contexts has been documented in prior studies ( Feng et al. 2016 ; Deftereos et al. 2015 ; Lin et al. 2014 ; Wang et al. 2019 ) . These genes provide biologically grounded probes for assessing spatial expression recovery.
blocks.zh: 聚合PCC为现位表达协议提供了有用的衡量标准,但它并没有揭示一个模型是否恢复基因表达的空间组织,如局部高表达区域,组织边界,以及区域强度变化. 因此,我们用标记基因的定性可视化来补充定量结果。 根据DKAN(张等人,2026年)中使用的生物标记可视化协议,我们可视化LCN2,GATA3,GPRC5A,和UBE2C,它们与相应癌症背景的相关性在之前的研究中都有记载(冯等人,2017年). 2016年; Deftereos et al. 2015; 林等编. 2014; 王等 2019 (中文(简体) ). 这些基因为评估空间表达恢复提供了基于生物的探测器.

For each method, we use the same fixed random seed, 42, to obtain a reproducible representative prediction. The seed is fixed uniformly across methods and is not tuned separately according to the marker-gene maps. The displayed examples are intended for qualitative inspection, whereas the quantitative claims in this paper are based on the five-seed aggregate results reported in Table 1 . The values in parentheses denote the PCC computed for the corresponding slide–gene pair and are included only to provide local quantitative context.

blocks.en: Across the displayed examples, HistoLoop more closely preserves the large-scale localization and regional intensity variation of the ground-truth maps, especially for GATA3, GPRC5A, and UBE2C. It also obtains the highest slide-level PCC in all four shown cases. We do not introduce a separate marker-gene PCC table because the aggregate comparison has already been reported in the main results.

blocks.en: Spatial Structure Preservation
blocks.zh: 空间结构保护

blocks.en: Gene-wise PCC evaluates the agreement of individual genes, but it does not directly measure whether the predicted profiles preserve multigene organization across spatial locations. Since expression-based clustering is commonly used to identify coherent tissue domains ( Zhu et al. 2024 ; Xiao et al. 2025 ) , we further evaluate the consistency of clusters derived from the predicted expression profiles.
blocks.zh: Gene-wise PCC评价单个基因的一致,但并不直接衡量预测剖面是否保留跨空间位置的多基因组织. 由于以表达为主的集群通常用于识别连贯的组织域(Zhu等人. 2024; Xiao et al. 2025),我们进一步评价了从预测的表达配置图中得出的集群的一致性.

blocks.en: For each held-out slide, we independently cluster the ground-truth and predicted expression profiles using the same clustering procedure and hyperparameters for every method. The resulting partitions are compared with the adjusted Rand index (ARI), adjusted mutual information (AMI), normalized mutual information (NMI), and homogeneity.
blocks.zh: 对于每个被搁置的幻灯片,我们使用同样的分组程序和每种方法的超参数,将地面真实和预测的表达剖面组合起来。 由此产生的分区与调整后的Rand指数(ARI),调整后的相互信息(AMI),正常化的相互信息(NMI),以及均匀性进行了比较.

blocks.en: Table 3: Overall clustering consistency between ground-truth and predicted expression profiles.
blocks.zh: 表3:地面真实度与预测表达特征之间的整体一致性。

blocks.en: Table 3 shows that HistoLoop achieves the highest score on all four metrics. Compared with the strongest baseline, HiST, HistoLoop improves ARI from 0.319 to 0.329, AMI from 0.479 to 0.526, NMI from 0.482 to 0.530, and homogeneity from 0.522 to 0.611. The consistent gains across metrics indicate that HistoLoop predictions preserve the multigene partition structure more faithfully than the competing methods under the same clustering protocol. This result complements the gene-wise PCC comparison by testing agreement at the profile and tissue-domain level.

blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.zh: 结论

blocks.en:
We presented HistoLoop, a looped Transformer for histology-based spatial gene expression prediction. HistoLoop progressively reconstructs multi-resolution spatial context from evolving spot states, allowing each refinement stage to use updated spatial evidence rather than relying on a fixed context representation. On HEST-1K, HistoLoop achieves the highest macro-averaged HVG50 PCC among the compared methods and obtains the best mean performance on four of the six cancer-specific tasks.
Controlled ablations highlight the contributions of recurrent
refinement, coarse-to-fine ordering, and state-dependent
context reconstruction. Complementary marker-gene visualizations and expression-derived clustering analyses indicate that the improvement extends beyond isolated gene-wise agreement to the recovery of spatially organized multigene patterns.
